_about: Single source of truth for every rendering, and the auditable term ledger (check 5). ONE rendering per referent for the whole book. Before you romanize any name, check here. status per entry: 'attested' (form used in English scholarship, give the citation in note), 'provisional' (your romanization, not found in outside sources), 'decided' (a project style call). If you find a better attested form mid-book, change it here AND grep every built chapter for the old form, then rebuild. Sections are top-level keys, rendered as glossary headings; keys starting with '_' are ignored. Rows nest UNDER a section: {section: {hanzi: {en, pinyin, status, note, ...}}}. apparatus_merge.py files each row under its 'category' field (default 'terms'). Add/rename sections freely (people, organizations, places, terms, ...).

林楠笙.cast: A Nationalist (Juntong) intelligence agent in occupied Shanghai; the novel's protagonist.
林楠笙.note: The protagonist; a Juntong agent. Pinyin.

朱怡贞.cast: A Communist intelligence agent and Lin Nansheng's first love; wife, in cover, of Ji Zhongyuan.
朱怡贞.note: A Communist agent; Lin's former student and lover. Endearment 贞贞, Zhenzhen. Pinyin.

顾慎言.cast: Lin Nansheng's superior and former training-class director; an elegant, cultivated spymaster.
顾慎言.note: Lin's superior and the director of studies of his training class. Pinyin.

左秋明.cast: A fellow trainee of Lin Nansheng's, now a Juntong liaison officer in Hong Kong.
左秋明.note: Lin's classmate from the training class; a liaison officer. Pinyin.

纪中原.cast: A Communist controller posing as a seal-engraver; Zhu Yizhen's husband in cover.
纪中原.note: Zhu Yizhen's controller and cover-husband; introduces himself as 'Old Ji.' Pinyin.

丁默邨.cast: A real turncoat: director of the No. 76 secret service of the Wang Jingwei regime.
丁默邨.note: Historical (1901–1947); Nationalist officer turned collaborator, co-founder of No. 76; executed as a traitor in 1947. Pinyin, the standard form in English scholarship.

铃木正男.note: The Japanese army surgeon who treats Lin in Hong Kong; addresses Lin as 'Pang-san.' Japanese reading.

小林大介.note: A second secretary at the Japanese consulate in Shanghai who trades intelligence with Lin. Japanese reading.

孟安南.note: An agent Gu Shenyan planted in Hong Kong years earlier; a member of the Indochinese Communist Party in cover. Pinyin.

童自重.note: A military-political adviser to the Wang regime; his Japanese army registry name is Uemura Kiyoshi (上村净). Assassinated at the Cathay Hotel. Pinyin.

蓝小姐.note: A celebrated Shanghai socialite (交际花) who serves as Lin's assistant in the assassination attempt. Pinyin of her surname.

老潘.note: The Communist contact who reactivates Zhu Yizhen after Ji Zhongyuan's presumed death. Pinyin.

汪精卫.note: Historical (1883–1944); leader of the Japanese-sponsored collaborationist government at Nanjing. Standard English form.

戴笠.note: Historical (1897–1946); head of the Juntong, the Nationalist military secret service. Called 'Mr. Dai' in the text. Standard English form.

军统.note: The Nationalists' military Bureau of Investigation and Statistics, Dai Li's secret service, seated in Chongqing. Attested English abbreviation.

中统.note: The Nationalist party's (CC Clique's) Bureau of Investigation and Statistics, the Juntong's civilian rival. Attested English abbreviation.

特工总部.note: The Wang regime's secret-service headquarters at No. 76 Jessfield Road.

新四军.note: A Communist army operating in central-eastern China; nominally allied with the Nationalists against Japan. Standard English form.

和平建国军.note: The Wang regime's armed forces, in full the Peace National Construction Army.

中美合作所.note: SACO, the joint Nationalist–US intelligence and training body (1943) under Dai Li and Milton Miles. Attested English name.

蓝衣社.note: The Blue Shirts Society, a fascist-influenced Nationalist secret organization tied to the Juntong. Attested English name.

特高课.note: The Japanese Special Higher Police (特別高等警察), the political and thought police. Attested English/Japanese term.

中储银行.note: The note-issuing bank of the Wang Jingwei regime.

华兴洋行.note: A silk-and-tea export firm; the Juntong's Shanghai intelligence relay in cover.

良友.note: The famous illustrated pictorial of Republican Shanghai (1926–1945). Attested English title.

大公报.note: A major, respected Chinese newspaper. Attested romanization.

中华日报.note: The chief newspaper of the Wang Jingwei regime.

中央日报.note: The Nationalist party's official newspaper. Attested English name.

路透社.note: The British news agency; Lin's journalistic cover. Attested English name.

朵云轩.note: The famous Shanghai studio for painting, calligraphy, and seal-carving (founded 1900). Attested romanization.

沪江大学.note: A Baptist missionary university in Shanghai (Hujiang University). Attested English name.

极司菲尔路.note: A road in western Shanghai, today's Wanhangdu Road; No. 76 stood here. Attested period English name.

愚园路.note: A fashionable road in western Shanghai. Attested form (per the translation shelf).

巨籁达路.note: A French Concession street lined with plane trees, today's Julu Road. Attested French name.

霞飞路.note: The main thoroughfare of the French Concession, today's Central Huaihai Road. Attested French name.

苏州河.note: The river through central Shanghai. Attested English form.

众坊街.note: A street in Yau Ma Tei, Hong Kong. Attested official English name.

洛克道.note: A street in Wan Chai, Hong Kong. Attested official English name.

大屿山.note: The large island west of Hong Kong. Attested English form.

广州湾.note: A French-leased territory on the Guangdong coast, today's Zhanjiang. Attested romanization.

启德机场.note: Hong Kong's airport. Attested English name.

重庆.note: The Nationalist wartime capital. Attested pinyin form (per the shelf).

华懋饭店.note: Victor Sassoon's Cathay Hotel on the Bund; today the north building of the Peace Hotel. Attested English name.

交际花.note: Literally 'a flower of society'; a fashionable woman of the demimonde who moves among wealthy men.

旗袍.note: The close-fitting Chinese woman's dress; 'cheongsam' is the established English form.

黄包车.note: The man-pulled two-wheeled cab of Republican Shanghai.

皖南事变.note: The Southern Anhui Incident of January 1941. Attested English name.

淞沪会战.note: The battle of August–November 1937. Attested English name.

整风运动.note: The Communist ideological campaign begun at Yan'an in 1942. Attested English name.

蝶恋花.note: An embroidery motif of butterflies among blossoms; also a classical song-lyric tune title.

咏梅.note: The title of the poem used as a contact signal; a 七律 (regulated verse).
